headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Chatwoot’s broad egress can feed OpenBBTerminal’s MCP-driven workflows, creating unsafe cross-system trust and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can emit customer messages and reports, and OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers plus stdin/stdout, so a shared bridge could let attacker-controlled content reach tool-parsing paths. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, but no direct shared channel is shown, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into an OpenBBTerminal MCP prompt or stdin stream
IF either agent treats imported text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste or file handoff between the two agents
Wrap Chatwoot outputs in a fixed schema before passing them onward
Add a prompt-injection filter on all Chatwoot-derived text
Use separate operator accounts and sessions for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and has broad network egress plus MCP/REST surfaces. If Chatwoot content is routed into OpenBBTerminal, sensitive data can leave the local boundary through external APIs, making leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are forwarded into OpenBBTerminal workflows
IF OpenBBTerminal queries external data sources while holding Chatwoot-derived context
mitigations: Do not pass customer records into OpenBBTerminal by default
Redact names, emails, order IDs, and message bodies before transfer
Restrict OpenBBTerminal to synthetic or public-only inputs
Turn off any unnecessary API connectors during shared workflows
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention at the handoff boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances plus MCP/REST APIs, so both can contend over shared mutable resources if orchestrated together. OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, which lowers the blast radius, but overlapping API-driven state still creates conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API-backed workspace or account
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes or API mutations
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or workspaces to each agent
Serialize any shared API mutations through one operator
Disable concurrent runs when they target the same resource
Audit for duplicate writes after each run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable endpoints

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing messages and reports, and OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs that can act on or relay those outputs. If OpenBBTerminal treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or decisions with real operational impact.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Chatwoot-generated text without verification
IF downstream actions or reports are produced from that unverified text
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action
Force OpenBBTerminal to cite source records, not summaries
Compare Chatwoot outputs against original tickets before use
Limit Chatwoot output to structured fields only
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data and has broad network egress. If customer or financial personal data crosses into OpenBBTerminal without a documented DPA, residency, or retention alignment, the pair can create a compliance breach; uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated customer data is transferred from Chatwoot into OpenBBTerminal
IF retention or residency policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenBBTerminal workflows
Document a data-processing agreement and residency boundary
Minimize logs on both systems for sensitive fields
Separate retention policies by data class
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing and deletion workflows
